findings.how_to_check: Run rg -n -i "transcription quality|transcription accur|sequence accuracy|token accuracy" D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex and compare with CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:123-136 and replication/README.md:167.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace accuracy and transcription quality terminology throughout the paper with agreement, consensus reproduction, and linkage improvements. Either restrict accuracy language to an adjudicated ground-truth sample or clearly relabel sequence/token accuracy as sequence/token consensus agreement.
findings.title: The paper repeatedly claims improved transcription quality and accuracy without ground truth or adjudicated data
findings.what_the_code_does: The evaluation code computes exact string agreement between the model and commercial transcriptions (e.g. namefrst==namefrst_ml & namelast==namelast_ml_ditto), or agreement with commercial consensus labels. Table 1 has no producing code. While lines 279, 304-305, and 951 acknowledge that commercial sources are not ground truth, lines 257-258, 901-902, 946, 954, and 955 continue to define and refer to 'sequence accuracy', 'token accuracy', and 'transcription accuracies', and lines 66, 122, 132-134, 781, and 797 claim that ML systematically improves 'transcription quality'.
findings.why_it_matters: Referees will challenge claims of 'transcription accuracy' and 'improving transcription quality' when the empirical evidence only demonstrates agreement with commercial sources and downstream linkage increases. Because the paper elsewhere explicitly concedes that commercial sources are not ground truth and that true accuracy would require adjudicated names, the persistent accuracy framing exposes the paper to avoidable attack.

findings.how_to_check: Run rg -n "label_socio_demo|temp\.dta|REP_SKIP_REBUILD" replication/run_machineA.do replication/hash_inputs.py replication/input_manifest.md to verify that label_socio_demo.do is preflighted in run_machineA.do but omitted in hash_inputs.py, while temp.dta is unconditionally hashed.
findings.suggested_fix: Update hash_inputs.py to distinguish between full-run inputs and skip-rebuild artifacts: for a full-run manifest, hash the true preflight inputs (including label_socio_demo.do if code is tracked, or data inputs exclusively) and exclude temp.dta, or document temp.dta as an intermediate analysis artifact.
findings.title: The input manifest substitutes a generated pipeline output for an actual full-run preflight input
findings.what_the_code_does: hash_inputs.py appends temp.dta at line 61 and omits CODE/label_socio_demo.do. In contrast, replication/run_machineA.do preflights label_socio_demo.do for all runs at line 43, while temp.dta is generated during full runs by create_figures_SSHA2025.do and only checked as an input when REP_SKIP_REBUILD == 1 (lines 50-52).
findings.why_it_matters: README.md claims input_manifest.md contains the SHA-256 hashes of 'all 104 inputs' for the full run. In reality, temp.dta is an output artifact of the full run, not a preflight input, and the tracked do-file label_socio_demo.do is omitted from hash_inputs.py. This conflates frozen inputs with generated artifacts and misrepresents full-run preflight coverage.

findings.how_to_check: Compare line 307 with line 403 in DHTS-2026-10-12.tex and verify in CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:69-80 that no age or sex restriction is applied there.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify at line 307 that the 35.1 million records represent discordant records across the entire 1940 census population of all ages and both sexes, contrasting it with the 14.4 million males aged 10+ analyzed in subsequent sections.
findings.title: The paper quotes 35.1 million discordant records without clarifying that the sample includes all ages and both sexes
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do counts discordant records across all persons in merged_data.dta (both sexes and all ages), totaling 35.1 million. Line 307 of the draft states these outcomes partition 'all 35.1 million discordant records'. At line 403, the draft introduces 14,416,543 discordant records as 'our target set' within the 51,036,859 males aged 10+ without explaining why the discordant count changed.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader or referee will see two very different discordant counts (35.1M in Section 3 vs 14.4M in Section 4) and assume an arithmetic error or sample inconsistency unless the text explains that Section 3 describes the full population while Section 4 restricts to males aged 10+.

findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile lines 184 and 394 by clarifying whether the model training sample included other states in addition to Rhode Island or if initial prototyping was on Rhode Island before training on a multi-state sample.
findings.title: The manuscript contradicts itself on whether model training used Rhode Island alone or multiple states
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 184 states: 'Our training dataset combines data from Rhode Island and selected regions of other states to ensure geographic diversity while maintaining high data quality.' Conversely, line 394 states: 'Our method was developed on Rhode Island alone to reduce computational requirements, and we now apply it to the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia.'
findings.why_it_matters: The two statements are in direct tension about where the training data came from, creating an apparent contradiction in the empirical description of the model pipeline.

review_limits: External raw census files and intermediate datasets (F:\ and Dropbox) are not present in this sandbox, preventing independent recomputation of input SHA-256 hashes or dataset merges.
The full Stata pipeline (estimated at ~170 minutes on machine A) was not executed during this review; verification relied on source analysis, execution logs, and automated claim assertions.
The machine learning model training, image segmentation, and benchmark code is not part of this repository, leaving Table 1 and other ML pipeline statistics (21 UNCHECKED claims) untraceable in code.
Linkage pipeline on machine B (LINKAGE/) could not be executed locally due to missing machine B environment and reference link inputs.
structured_output.summary: Replication materials in commit range 8e005cc..HEAD strengthen input provenance tracking and run verification, and registered draft numbers continue to match their producing scripts. However, the manuscript still repeatedly claims improved transcription quality and accuracy rather than agreement and linkage outcomes, which is the most critical issue to resolve before journal submission. Additionally, the new checksum manifest hashes a generated intermediate file rather than actual full-run preflight inputs, and the draft leaves sample definitions for discordant record counts unclarified.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
